Truth is for nourishment, concepts are for play. The mind is like a cat in a kings pantry, and concepts little mice coming to nibble at the goods in the kings stores, which when caught are roughly toyed with, victims of a succumbing to bestial delights, until limp and lifeless they are made, but it's all fun and games for the cat. It even likes it when they pretend to be dead, just for the surprise of another spurt of furtive contention. But Truth is the king's feast, set out upon his long table, brought from his compound's deep stores by beings he barely cares to notice, so important is his nourishment and delight. Sometimes he lets his cat up to the table for a nibble, but little of the feast ever can it stomach, though it will gnaw away happily for some while.
